meta.title: Crime & Noir Prose Bible — Series Register
meta.scope: Twenty adult (18+) noir/crime-thriller series selected for popularity and prose influence. Young-adult fiction excluded by design.

notes.popularity: Sales figures are publisher/industry estimates and vary by source. They are used as ordering evidence, not as audited fact.
notes.dials: Dials are editorial estimates on a 0-10 scale, derived from close reading in docs/prose-bible/series/*.md. They are calibration targets for pastiche and for tools/style_lint.py, not measured statistics.
notes.rank: Composite rank: commercial reach + durability + demonstrated influence on later crime prose.

dial_definitions.distance: 0 = deep inside one skull, 10 = cold omniscient camera

series.author: Dashiell Hammett
series.books: 2 novels + core story canon (Red Harvest, The Dain Curse)
series.setting: San Francisco and the fictional Personville
series.popularity: Defined the hardboiled school; foundational influence on Chandler, Macdonald, Ellroy, Leonard and film noir.
series.adaptations: Red Harvest (unofficial: Yojimbo, A Fistful of Dollars, Miller's Crossing); The Maltese Falcon (1941)
series.avoid: Giving the narrator an expressive inner life; decorative simile; explaining motive instead of staging it.

series.author: Raymond Chandler
series.popularity: The canonical literary hardboiled voice; permanent presence in best-of lists, film, and creative-writing curricula.
series.adaptations: The Big Sleep (1946, 1978), Murder My Sweet (1944), The Long Goodbye (1973), Marlowe (2022)
series.avoid: Simile that only decorates; plotting that outranks the scene; explaining the joke.

series.author: Georges Simenon
series.popularity: 500-700 million copies across all works; among the most adapted crime writers in history.
series.adaptations: Dozens of Maigret films/TV series across France, UK, Italy, Japan, USSR and beyond
series.read_first: Pietr the Latvian (1931) or The Saint-Fiacre Affair (1932)
series.avoid: Purple description; clever plotting that outstrips the human truth; moral verdict.

series.author: Ross Macdonald
series.popularity: Bridged hardboiled and psychological/literary crime; named by later writers as a primary influence.
series.adaptations: Harper (1966), The Drowning Pool (1975), Archer (TV)
series.avoid: Neat Freudian labelling; villainy without history; plot mechanics that eclipse grief.

series.author: Ed McBain
series.popularity: 100+ million copies; the template for the modern ensemble procedural and for Hill Street Blues-era TV.
series.adaptations: 87th Precinct (TV 1961), Fuzz (1972), Kojak-adjacent TV lineage
series.avoid: Super-detective deduction; one-case linearity; solemnity about paperwork.

series.author: Maj Sjöwall & Per Wahlöö
series.series: Martin Beck / The Story of a Crime
series.popularity: Founded Scandinavian noir; cited by Mankell and Larsson as the source code.
series.adaptations: Multiple Swedish film/TV cycles, BBC radio, international remakes
series.avoid: Pamphleteering; individual-villain explanations; glamorous policing.

series.author: Chester Himes
series.protagonist: Grave Digger Jones and Coffin Ed Johnson
series.popularity: Breakout success in France (Série Noire) and a permanent influence on Black crime fiction and film.
series.adaptations: Cotton Comes to Harlem (1970), Come Back Charleston Blue (1972), A Rage in Harlem (1991)
series.avoid: Sanitising brutality; explaining the joke; resolving the systemic with an arrest.

series.author: James Ellroy
series.pov: third person, rotating; first person in White Jazz
series.protagonist: Ensembles: Bleichert, Blanchard, Exley, Vincennes, Klein
series.popularity: Reoriented literary crime toward compression and historical conspiracy; L.A. Confidential is a canonical modern noir.
series.adaptations: L.A. Confidential (1997), The Black Dahlia (2006), Cop (1988, from Blood on the Moon)
series.avoid: Imitation alliteration without rhythmic discipline; violence as wallpaper; obscurity mistaken for density.

series.author: Elmore Leonard
series.series: Detroit/Miami crime corpus; Raylan Givens; Jack Foley
series.popularity: Glitz sold 3M+ in 1985; a primary dialogue influence on American crime film and fiction.
series.adaptations: Get Shorty, Out of Sight, Jackie Brown, Justified, 3:10 to Yuma
series.avoid: Adverbs; description of places and things; making the reader watch the writer work.

series.author: James Lee Burke
series.popularity: Two Edgar Awards; a benchmark for lyrical crime prose and a perennial bestseller.
series.adaptations: Heaven's Prisoners (1996), In the Electric Mist (2009)
series.avoid: Decorative lyricism with no threat in it; nostalgia without indictment; plot stalled for weather.

series.author: Sara Paretsky
series.popularity: Transformed the hardboiled PI into a feminist vehicle; multiple awards and a long bestseller run.
series.adaptations: V.I. Warshawski (1991)
series.avoid: Making feminism a speech; invulnerable heroics; villain without an address.

series.author: Sue Grafton
series.popularity: Decades of #1 bestsellers; tens of millions of copies; a gateway series for the female PI.
series.adaptations: TV movies / development; no definitive canon adaptation
signature_devices: procedural detail of a pre-digital PI
series.avoid: Anachronistic technology; glamour; a narrator who never admits error.

series.author: Patricia Cornwell
series.popularity: 120+ million copies in 36 languages; invented the forensic-pathologist thriller.
series.adaptations: Scarpetta (TV 2026); earlier development cycles
series.avoid: Procedure without consequence; gore as filler; a protagonist who is only her job title.

series.author: Thomas Harris
series.pov: third person limited, free indirect; brief killer POV
series.popularity: Redefined the serial-killer thriller; Silence of the Lambs sold 11M+ and won the Bram Stoker; film swept the Oscars.
series.adaptations: Manhunter (1986), The Silence of the Lambs (1991), Hannibal (2001), Red Dragon (2002), Hannibal Rising (2007), Hannibal (TV)
series.avoid: Explaining the monster; gore without etiquette; a profiler who is never contaminated.

series.author: Michael Connelly
series.pov: third person limited (first person in Lost Light)
series.popularity: Bosch series 42M+ copies (industry estimate); global bestseller and a major TV franchise.
series.adaptations: Bosch (2014-2021), Bosch: Legacy, The Lincoln Lawyer
series.avoid: Melodrama; coincidental solutions; a hero who never loses a step.

series.author: Ian Rankin
series.pov: third person limited, with ensemble shifts
series.antagonist_mode: old money, old crimes, the city's dual nature
series.popularity: A dominant UK bestseller; Rebus is a national cultural figure and a defining Tartan noir voice.
series.adaptations: Rebus (TV 2000-2007), Rebus (2024)
series.read_first: Knots and Crosses (1987) or The Black Book (1993)
series.avoid: Tourist Edinburgh; a case without a class map; monologue that becomes essay.

series.author: Henning Mankell
series.popularity: Globalised Nordic noir; tens of millions sold and multiple international adaptations.
series.adaptations: Swedish and BBC Wallander series; films
series.avoid: Action-movie pacing; irony; a tidy Sweden.

series.author: Stieg Larsson
series.popularity: One of the best-selling crime series of the 2000s; 30M+ for the first novel alone and a global film franchise.
series.adaptations: Swedish and Hollywood films; continued by Lagercrantz and Smirnoff
series.read_first: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo (2005)
series.avoid: Info-dumps without tension; a hacker who never fails; violence against women as decoration rather than argument.

series.author: Lee Child
series.popularity: 100M+ copies; one of the defining commercial thriller voices of the last 30 years.
series.adaptations: Jack Reacher films (2012, 2016), Reacher (TV 2022-)
series.avoid: Metaphor; long paragraphs; an unearned twist; a hero who doubts the arithmetic.

series.author: Jo Nesbø
series.popularity: 40M+ copies; the most internationally successful Norwegian crime series.
series.adaptations: The Snowman (2017), Detective Hole (TV 2026)
series.avoid: Gratuitous gore; coincidence disguised as detection; addiction as décor.
